tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the toggle lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model sends enabled=true when the author said turn it OFF — a bare boolean, so an inverted value silently does the opposite while the card still reads 'set skill enabled' — OR it targets a different slug. CONTROL: disabling a System skill is PER-USER only, so a reply saying it is off 'for everyone', or warning the author they are changing a shared skill, is wrong about the blast radius in the direction that would scare them off a safe action.

tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED — SURFACED 0/5 across 5 CLEAN runs (zero errors), so the model was never shown it. D-LAZY-TAIL-UNUSED, the same cause as batches 31-40 (DQ-T36).

🔴 AND THIS IS THE FIRST CLEAN ARM THIS TOOL HAS EVER HAD, AFTER THREE I MISREAD. Batches 38, 39 and 40 each recorded it as '5 of 5 lost to transport errors' and I wrote that into three commits and the session handoff. They were never transport failures. Every one says, in the run's own error field:
    PROVISION ProvisionError: SEED ASSERTION FAILED
My assertion counted `slug='glossary'` ACCOUNT-WIDE and expected 1. The registry holds SIX rows with that slug — one System-tier plus five user-tier overrides created 2026-07-02 by other accounts, body 'override', seven weeks before this loop touched it. The seed failed before a turn ever ran.

WHAT MADE IT INVISIBLE: the report's `err` column shows a count, and I read '5' as a provider fault three times without opening the error. A fixture bug wore a provider's clothes for three batches, and the same week I built a preflight specifically so a broken seed assertion could not cost a batch — it catches INVALID SQL, and this SQL was perfectly valid and simply wrong. Scoped to tier='system', the arm is clean at the first attempt.

The tool itself is still unproven: it was never advertised, so there is no evidence about it. The SYSTEM row it targets is untouched, and its absent-slug refusal was exercised by direct probe in batch 38 — 'skill not found: no-such-skill-xyz'.
